bugs: main.py catches SyntaxError but CompileError (raised by compiler) is not a SyntaxError, so compiler errors (e.g., missing brace) cause unhandled exception instead of a formatted error message.
Lexer raises SyntaxError as plain string without lineno attribute, so main.py cannot extract meaningful line number; error messages will lack line numbers.
VirtualMachine runtime errors (e.g., division by zero, undefined variable) are raised without a line number; the Code object has no debug line mapping, so line numbers cannot be reported.

final_review.suggestions: 1. Create main.py that reads sys.argv[1], lexes, compiles, runs, and catches both SyntaxError (from lexer/compiler) and RuntimeError_, printing line numbers. 2. Add example programs (calculator.yal, factorial.yal, fibonacci.yal) in an examples/ directory. 3. In lexer.py, change invalid-character raise to `raise SyntaxError(f'Unexpected character...', (None, start_line, None, None))`. 4. In compiler.py, change `class CompileError(SyntaxError): pass` and raise with `(msg, (None, token.line, None, None))` to set lineno. 5. Add a `lines` list to Code class; in compiler, pass current line to emit(); in VM, retrieve line from frame.code.lines[frame.ip] when raising RuntimeError_. 6. In VM, for COMPARE_OP with <, >, <=, >=, add numeric operand checks like in _check_numeric, raising RuntimeError_ with line info.
